activity_summary: You ate by the Monday copper. Galls, copperas, and gum. The loaf was a penny and a finger and a half short of the notch, and nobody weighed it. Board was threepence. You told them Alice's bill and did not divide it. You said the afternoon is Titus, an old Roman, done by the fourth act.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Ate, kept Sunday's bill undivided, and named the afternoon's part.

entities.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell
entities.context: Boiled the Monday ink, measured the loaf by eye, and took threepence.

entities.name: Alse Pinder
entities.context: Stirred the gum and asked whether he played.

entities.name: Gillis Verbeke
entities.context: Came in for bread, and did not weigh the loaf.

facets.activity: Ate by the Monday copper and named the old Roman

quotes.speaker: dorcas_ansell
quotes.text: A finger and a half to the hair, and a penny paid at the bakehouse door.

quotes.speaker: william_shakespeare
quotes.text: Titus, at two. An old Roman.
